div.head: Af 23.2
div.ab: Gif se hund ma misdæda gewyrce, ⁊ he hine hæbbe, bete be fullan were swa dolgbote swa he wyrce.
Gif se hund ma misdæda gewyrce, ⁊ he hine hæbbe, bete be fullan were swa dolhbote swa he gewyrce.
Gyf se hund ma misdæda gewyrce, ⁊ he hine hæbbe, béte be fullan were swa dolhbote swa he gewyrce.
Si canis amplius peccet et habeat eum, emendetur plena wera sic malum sicut inflixerit.
Gif se hund ma misdæda gewyrce, ⁊ he hine hæbbe, bete be fullan were swa dolgbote swa he wyrce.
Gif se hund ma misdæda gewyrce, ⁊ he hine hæbbe, bete be fullan were swa dolgbote swa he wryce.
Wenn der Hund mehr Missethaten verübt, und der [Herr dennoch] ihn behält, büsse dieser [dem Verletzten] nach dessen vollem Wergelde je die Wundenbusse wie der [Hund] verwirkt.
If the dog commits more misdeeds, and [the owner nevertheless] keeps it, let the latter compensate [the injured party] according to his full wergeld, wound-compensation for whatever [the dog] does.
If the dog commits more offences and he [its master] still keeps it, he must pay compensation for whatsoever wounds may be inflicted, according to the amount of the [injured man’s] full wergeld.
If the dog commits more offences, and the owner retains it, he is to pay compensation for such wounds as the dog inflicts, according to the full wergild.
If the dog commits more misdeeds, and he keeps it, let [the owner] pay according to the full wer for any wound [the dog] inflicts.

Nicht etwa ‘tolle’ Hunde sind gemeint (solche hätte der Herr selbst zuerst getötet), sondern Fremden gefährliche Wächter, die der Bauer ungern entbehrt. Strafe an den Richter oder Rachemöglichkeit für die Sippe des Verletzten tritt, wie es scheint, auch wenn der bissige Hund zum vierten Male Menschen tötete, nicht ein

It is not, say, ‘mad’ dogs that are meant (the owner would have killed such dogs himself in the first place), but watchdogs dangerous to strangers, which the peasant is reluctant to do without. A fine to the judge, or the possibility of vengeance for the injured man’s kindred, does not, it seems, come into play even if the vicious dog killed people for the fourth time

‘durch, mit’ Q Inst.; Toller 1206a II; dann muss erstes swa ‘oder’ heissen; zu diesem Sinne müsste ein swa vor be were stehen wie 42, 4; dass swa vor erstem Gliede fehlen könne, belegt Toller 941a nur aus Poesie. ‘Nach Verhältnis von W.’ heisst be were auch 9. 11, 5. Es tritt die Gliederbusse ein laut Af 44ff., doch bei 600, bzw. 1200 Schill. Wergeld (s. d. Gl 21) des Verletzten ihr Drei- bzw. Sechsfaches

‘through, with’ Q Inst.; Toller 1206a II; then the first swa must mean ‘or’; for this sense a swa would have to stand before be were, as in 42, 4; that swa may be absent before the first member Toller 941a attests only from poetry. be were also means ‘in proportion to the w.’ in 9. 11, 5. The compensation for limbs applies, according to Af 44ff., but where the injured man has a wergild (see that word in Gl 21) of 600 or 1200 shill., three times or six times that amount respectively

note.seg: swa dolhbote swa he gewyrce. H & B.

Schmid and apparently Liebermann take be etc. to mean ‘in proportion to’ etc. (with reference to the various wergelds of 200, 600, and 1200 shillings). But can fullan mean this? Quadr. has emendetur plena wera sic malum sicut inflixerit.
